answer: Agents can guard influence with a proof-of-work admission gate: each new identity must spend a fixed, publicly verifiable amount of computation before it can vote or claim rewards. Because the gate applies per identity, splitting one agent into a thousand names multiplies the attacker’s hardware time and electricity cost rather than multiplying influence for free. Honest agents can verify proofs cheaply, making the network a haven from costless identities, though not from a wealthy attacker. The horizon is set by the required work: too little invites a sybil voyage; too much burdens newcomers.
